title: Quarterly flight deck: Hosted endpoints readiness, rotation lanes and contingency playbook
creator: Rina Patel
description: Objective: Produce a single-quarter ‘flight deck’ that defines commitment lanes for hosted endpoints and the model catalog, with explicit rotation windows, canary gating criteria, contingency fallback families, cost/latency guardrails, and cross-functional runbooks. Deliverables: 1) Commitment matrix that maps feature endpoints to model families (primary, warm-fallback, cold-fallback) and target SLOs; 2) Canary gating thresholds (quality regression, P95 latency, token cost delta) and automated rollback rules; 3) Contingency playbook with capacity hedges and burst policies for Dedicated customers; 4) Runbook snippets for Console pages to highlight model health and token cost drift; 5) Stakeholder sign-off checklist for PM/Eng/Design/SRE prior to any model rotation. Scope: Hosted API endpoints + model catalog decisions for the quarter. Excludes on-prem private deployment script changes (tracked separately). Success metrics: no more than one customer-facing regression tied to model rotation during the quarter; average token-cost delta across rotated endpoints <= +8%; canary false-positive rate < 5% (alerts that triggered but later deemed benign).
acceptance_criteria: Commitment matrix published in Confluence with ownership and rollout windows
Canary gating automated in CI with thresholds configured in staging and test canaries
Runbook entries added to Console doc links and validated in a tabletop exercise
Cross-functional sign-off recorded (PM, ENG, SRE, Design) before first rotation
Fallback model families validated on a synthetic workload with latency and cost targets
decisions: Adopt a 3-tier fallback family model: primary (best quality), warm-fallback (quantized lower-cost variant), cold-fallback (smaller family)
Require both quality and latency gates to pass in canary; failing either triggers staged rollback
Use per-route token-cost delta (+%) as a soft signal for rollback but not sole decision driver

notes: Trade-offs discussed: aggressive rotation accelerates model improvements but raises regression risk; mitigation chosen prioritizes two-stage canary with automatic rollback and manual override
